name: Airtel
summary: Airtel (Bharti Airtel) provides mobile, broadband, DTH and enterprise connectivity services in India, and hires for sales and distribution, network, technology, marketing and customer roles, plus graduates from campuses. Candidates commonly report functional or technical interviews alongside behavioural questions, and Airtel publishes three core values it calls AIR: Alive, Inclusive and Respectful.
rounds: Online assessment or aptitude test for some graduate and entry-level roles
Functional or technical interview with the hiring team
Case discussion or group exercise for some campus programmes
Hiring manager or senior leader interview
looks_for: Alive: energy, a can-do attitude, and finding a way when something seems impossible
Inclusive: championing diversity and adapting to the needs of very different communities
Focus on the customer in sales, service and network work
Commercial sense about distribution, retail and market share in a territory
Analytical thinking with data on usage, churn and network quality

questions.text: Tell me about a time someone said something couldn't be done and you found a way.
covers: What was said to be impossible, and why
The approach you found and the risk you took
The result, with a number if possible

questions.text: Describe a time you worked with people very different from you to get a result.
covers: How they differed: background, language, function or seniority
What you adjusted in how you worked or communicated
What you achieved together

questions.text: Tell me about a time you admitted a mistake openly. What happened next?
covers: The mistake and why you chose to raise it
Who you told and how you fixed it
What it did for trust, and what you learned

questions.text: Tell me about a time you went out of your way for a customer.
covers: Who the customer was and what they needed
What you did beyond the usual
The outcome for the customer and for the business

questions.text: Postpaid customers in one circle are leaving faster than usual. How would you find out why and win them back?
covers: Who is leaving: segment, tenure, plan, area
Likely reasons: network quality, price, billing issues, competitor offers
Retention actions to test, and how you'd measure whether they worked

questions.text: How would you grow broadband connections in a city where a competitor is strong?
covers: Where to focus: areas with fibre coverage, new buildings, unhappy customers
The offer: speed, bundles, installation time, service
Channels and the metrics to track: connections, installs, early churn

questions.text: You manage distributors and retailers in a territory, and SIM sales are falling. What would you do in your first month?
covers: Visiting the market and talking to retailers before deciding
Checking stock, schemes, competition and retailer coverage
A short plan with weekly targets, and how you'd follow it up

questions.text: Explain what a mobile tower site needs to work, and what commonly causes outages.
covers: Radio equipment, antennas, power with backup, and a transmission link
Common causes: power failure, fibre cuts, hardware faults, weather
How monitoring and quick field response reduce downtime

questions.text: How would you build a model that flags customers likely to leave, and what would you do with that list?
covers: Useful signals: usage drop, complaints, network issues, plan changes
A simple model first, checked on past data
Turning scores into actions, and testing that the actions reduce churn

questions.text: How would you estimate the number of smartphone users in Lucknow?
covers: Population, then the share by age group who use a phone
The share of those with a smartphone
Rounded numbers, stated assumptions and a sanity check

questions.text: An enterprise client's leased line keeps dropping. How would you manage the issue and the relationship?
covers: Acknowledging the impact and naming one point of contact
Working with the network team on the root cause, not just restoring service
Regular updates and a review once it's fixed

questions.text: Explain ARPU and churn, and why a telecom company watches them closely.
covers: ARPU: average revenue per user over a period
Churn: the share of customers who leave
How the two together drive revenue growth, with a simple example

questions.text: Why Airtel? Which of its values, Alive, Inclusive or Respectful, do you relate to most?
covers: A reason tied to Airtel's services or the role
One value with a short, real example
What you want to learn in your first years

questions.text: Are you comfortable starting in a field sales or circle role, possibly outside your home city?
covers: An honest answer about moving and field work
Why time in the market would help you
Any past experience in sales or on the ground

tips: Know the telecom metrics: ARPU, churn, subscriber growth, network availability and customer satisfaction.
For sales roles, understand distribution: distributors, retailers, activations and recharges.
Prepare one story for each AIR value; Alive suits stories of finding a way around an obstacle.
Use Airtel's products (prepaid, postpaid, broadband, DTH, Airtel Business) as examples so your case answers stay concrete.
